svg.title: At a well-child visit a mother says her 2-month-old “cries all the time.” Which action should the nurse take first?
svg.desc: Assess before you act. A healthy infant cries 1 to 3 hours a day — it is how they say hungry, thirsty, tired, wet or hurting — so “all the time” means nothing until you know the pattern, frequency and quality . Calling the provider first skips the data that would make the call useful. Carrying on with the check-in dismisses a parent's concern for the sake of the schedule , and calling it normal without asking is the same dismissal in kinder words. What the quality tells you: a high-pitched, shrill cry is a neurologic sign — raised intracranial pressure until proven otherwise — and that one is reported straight away. Which is exactly why the nurse asks first.
